revisionHistory.summary: The page host moved into the registry. No product decision changed.
retainedTraits: every owner, contract, prop, fixture and state from 1.0

revisionHistory.reason: Apply could not materialize 1.0: the target canon lint reported 6 errors, two of them structural. A new registry key was needed, which changes the approved artifact and therefore requires a new revision rather than an Apply-time repair.
revisionHistory.visibleDifference: The column is WIDER. max-w-4xl is not a member of LayoutClassName, so the admitted key carries max-w-6xl. Content, order, states and tones are unchanged.

revisionHistory.summary: The route is named in English and the copy moved into the message catalogue. No layout, order, tone or state changed.
retainedTraits: every owner, contract, prop, state and tone from 1.1
rejectedTraits: the route segment `cap-phat` - starci-fe/no-second-language-in-path refuses a romanised second language in a path, and a route is the address a customer quotes and an import repeats
sentences written at the call site - the same term ended up spelled differently on two screens and a second language would have meant editing every file that renders a word
a `listFactLoading` catalogue key - the surface draws a skeleton over that slot, so it was a string no reader could ever see and a translator would have maintained forever
revisionHistory.reason: The owner asked for i18n, for the provisioning screen to carry no Vietnamese in its names, and for the naming rule to say so. NAMING-3 now says it and the trust tree tests it, so 1.1 no longer passes its own gate.
revisionHistory.visibleDifference: None on screen. The rendered Vietnamese is identical; it now arrives from apps/app/src/messages/vi.json instead of from constants in the page, and the same fixture renders in English from en.json.

revisionHistory.summary: The page owner left the routing tree. Nothing on screen changed.
retainedTraits: every owner, contract, prop, state, tone and word from 1.2 - the four screenshots are byte-identical
rejectedTraits: a page owner under `app/` - LAYOUT-6 says a file there names which page renders at which URL and nothing else, and the routing tree is addressed by URL rather than browsed by tier, so a component parked there is invisible to everyone looking for it beside its siblings
the name `fleet-page.tsx` - the folder is the component's name, so `components/pages/ProvisioningPage/index.tsx` makes the path predict the name
revisionHistory.reason: The owner caught it at the Apply confirmation. It had reached that point with every gate green because LAYOUT-6 was prose that no rule read; `starci-fe/route-tree-holds-routes-only` now reads it, and the same sweep moved every other page in the workspace out of its routing tree.
revisionHistory.visibleDifference: None, and that is provable rather than asserted: the populated, empty and error screenshots hash identically to 1.2's.

revisionHistory.summary: The fixture is declared as a target. Nothing on screen changed.
retainedTraits: every owner, contract, prop, state, tone and word from 1.3 - the populated, empty and error screenshots are byte-identical
rejectedTraits: a candidate.files list that omitted the fixture the page imports - 1.3 named two targets and the page needed three, so Apply could not write it without inventing a path for the third, which is precisely the improvisation the seal exists to prevent
`src/fixtures/` as the fixture's home - a page folder may hold only its two halves and their twins, and `resources/` is where a config map already belongs in this tree
revisionHistory.reason: Apply stopped before its first write. The page imports a fixture that the sealed record never gave a target, and the Apply law is explicit that an edit nobody declared before the seal returns to Preview rather than being written and explained afterwards.
revisionHistory.visibleDifference: None. Only the target map and the fixture's path changed; the populated, empty and error captures hash identically to 1.3's.

unknowns: The review chrome first served the candidate from a subpath, where Next's absolute asset paths 404 and the frame rendered unstyled. Fixed by giving the candidate its own origin; the sealed screenshots are from that origin.
Whether ContractChildSpec needs a fourth kind for blocks. fleet-resource-list declares composite: "fleet-row" while FleetRow's meta.shape is "block".
Whether one user may hold more than one agent workspace; the query name is singular and its response is an array.

Pointing the next-intl plugin at the app's request config was tried in the candidate and fails at prerender: getTranslations needs a request scope a static export never enters. The candidate therefore passes the catalogue to the client provider directly, over the same vi.json file.

decisions.decision: Preview's write boundary was widened to packages/ui/src/contracts/index.ts and packages/ui/src/blocks/
decisions.tradeoff: deviates from CONTEXT-LOCK-6, which makes Preview artifact-only; taken because a closed ContractKey union makes a new row anatomy impossible to express inside the artifact

decisions.decision: kind and status are two badges, not one
decisions.tradeoff: one more element per row; without it a suspended resource reads as a different kind of thing from a running one

decisions.decision: the row action slot is optional rather than disabled
decisions.tradeoff: the row's right edge is ragged across states; a disabled button would promise a control that does not exist

decisions.decision: two unprefixed layout class names were admitted into LayoutClassName
decisions.tradeoff: the union grew by two; the md: twins already existed and a row whose first child takes the slack at every width needs them unprefixed

files.note: the page owner; holds all four states and resolves every label through useTranslations("provisioning"). One file rather than two per SPLIT-6: the split exists because a request exists, and this screen still reads a fixture.
the route. It mounts the page and nothing else, which is the whole of what a file under app/ may do.

the stand-in for the query that does not exist yet. It carries KEYS, never words, so the same file renders in either locale. 1.3 imported it and never said where it lands, which is why Apply could not write the page without inventing a path.

notPorted.reason: REVIEW ROUTE. Isolates the empty state so it can be photographed at a stable URL. The app reaches the same state from data, not from a route.
REVIEW ROUTE. Same reason, for the pending state.
REVIEW ROUTE. Same reason, for the query-failed state - which is not the same thing as a resource whose status is failed.

The app already has a layout, and it is BETTER than this one: it resolves its title through getTranslations, which a static export cannot run. Porting this would replace a request-time shell with a build-time one.

The app already has its providers, and they read the catalogue through the next-intl plugin. The candidate passes messages explicitly because a static export has no request scope - a difference in mechanism only, over the same vi.json.
The app already has it. The candidate's copy differs only in `@source` depth, because it sits six directories further down.
MUST NOT BE PORTED. It carries `output: "export"`, which is what makes the build hashable and what would turn the production app into a static site if it landed.

i18n.note: The fixture carries KEYS - `kind`, `status` and `action` are catalogue names, not words - so one fixture renders in either locale. The candidate imports the app's own catalogue rather than holding a copy.

integrationEdits.reason: three imports become the app's own specifiers on materialization, and nothing else in the file changes. StatRow is reached by relative path into packages/ui/src because @nivo/ui's exports map publishes only ., ./contracts, ./leaves/* and ./branches/*, so it becomes @nivo/ui/composites/StatRow once the map admits it. FleetRow and the fixture are reached by relative path because the candidate sits outside the app; both become @/ aliases.
the candidate's route reaches the page by relative path because it sits inside the lab; in the app it becomes the @/ alias.
the exports map must admit ./composites/* before the StatRow import above can be a specifier
